# seqout

> Python and R clients for seqout.org, a metadata index over NCBI GEO, NCBI SRA, EBI ENA, DDBJ (DRA and GEA), ArrayExpress and GSA (CNCB-NGDC). Search every archive at once, resolve an accession to its records in the others, and read GEO supplementary files as counts matrices.

The two clients are independent and versioned separately. Both answer from either
DuckDB over remote Parquet files at https://seqout.org/data, or the REST API at
https://seqout.org/api. The backend is always chosen explicitly.

Install:

```bash
uv add seqout                    # Python library, needs Python 3.13+
uv add 'seqout[counts]'          # with the counts-matrix readers
uv tool install seqout           # the seqout command line
```

```r
pak::pak("saketlab/seqout/R")                                              # R package
install.packages("seqout", repos = "https://saketlab.r-universe.dev")      # or r-universe
```

The development version installs from GitHub. The Python package lives in the
`python/` subdirectory of the repo, so `#subdirectory=python` is required.

```bash
uv add "seqout @ git+https://github.com/saketlab/seqout.git#subdirectory=python"
```

Python:

```python
from seqout import connect, seqout_counts

sq = connect()
sq.search("liver cancer scRNA", organism="Homo sapiens")
sq.get("GSE151530").samples

counts = seqout_counts(gse="GSE297547")
counts.manifest()                        # readable units, nothing downloaded yet
counts.matrix(sample="GSM8994520")       # AnnData, cells by genes
counts.design                            # one row per sample
```

R:

```r
library(seqout)

con <- seqout_connect()
find_projects(con, keywords = "liver cancer scRNA", organism = "Homo sapiens")
project_samples(con, "GSE151530")

counts <- seqout_counts(con, "GSE297547")
manifest(counts)
seqout_matrix(counts, sample = "GSM8994520")
```

## Documentation

- [Overview](https://seqout.org/cli/): both clients, install commands and a worked example
- [Python client](https://seqout.org/cli/python/): library, command line and Parquet backend
- [Python installation](https://seqout.org/cli/python/installation/): pip, uv and the optional extras
- [Command line](https://seqout.org/cli/python/cli/): every verb of the `seqout` command, with options
- [Python library](https://seqout.org/cli/python/library/): `connect()`, `Dataset` and the client method surface
- [Parquet backend](https://seqout.org/cli/python/parquet/): querying the Parquet dump with DuckDB, offline or in place
- [Counts matrices](https://seqout.org/cli/python/reference/counts/): `seqout_counts`, manifests, units and readers
- [R package](https://seqout.org/cli/R/): reference index and articles
- [R function reference](https://seqout.org/cli/R/reference/): every exported function, grouped by task
- [Getting started in R](https://seqout.org/cli/R/articles/getting-started.html): connecting, searching, and reading a study
- [Counts and metadata in R](https://seqout.org/cli/R/articles/counts-and-metadata.html): GEO supplementary files to a Seurat object

## Examples

- [Getting started](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/01_getting_started/): connecting, searching with filters, reading a dataset
- [Working with a dataset](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/02_working_with_a_dataset/): every field a `Dataset` holds
- [Accessions and archives](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/03_accessions_and_archives/): how an accession from any archive resolves, and when it cannot
- [Offline with Parquet](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/04_offline_with_parquet/): the same data with no API request, and where that backend stops
- [Counts and metadata](https://seqout.org/cli/python/examples/05_counts_and_metadata/): a counts matrix with per-cell annotation and study metadata joined in

## Optional

- [Metadata normalization](https://seqout.org/cli/python/normalization/): `--norm`, which labels free-text GEO sample fields with a local language model
- [Source](https://github.com/saketlab/seqout): both clients, MIT licensed
- [Issues](https://github.com/saketlab/seqout/issues)
- [seqout.org](https://seqout.org): the web interface over the same data
